html:
SMTO-ART-0005 — SMTO can't reach the saved files for this Task

GUID: 67d4f536-782b-442c-a176-1c45fe1144ab
Slug: artifact-workspace-unavailable
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't open the place where it keeps this Task's saved files. They may have been deleted, a scheduled cleanup may be checking them, or the server can't read its storage right now.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a minute, then select Artifacts from this run for the Task again. SMTO briefly holds a Task's files while its hourly cleanup checks them, and they come back when that check ends.
  2. Open the conversation's Retention menu, choose Artifact retention settings, and look at the retention choice and the Last cleanup line. A 7, 30 or 90 day setting, or someone choosing Delete artifacts or Delete everything, removes Task files on purpose.
  3. If the error says storage is temporarily unavailable, ask the person who manages SMTO to make sure the server computer has free disk space and its data drive is connected. SMTO keeps saved files on the server's disk and can't open them if that disk is full, missing or blocked.

What success looks like

  • The Artifacts from this run list opens and shows the Task's files, or clearly says the files from this run have been deleted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete or move SMTO's data folder; your saved files may still be inside it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The run's artifact workspace could not be accessed: its namespace is missing or retired, a maintenance cleanup claim is held on it, or listing, reading or exporting hit an OS storage error.

What this means

  • Workspace lookup finds missing/retired namespace or active cleanup, or artifact read/list/download catches an OS/storage access failure. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Workspace lookup finds missing/retired namespace or active cleanup, or artifact read/list/download catches an OS/storage access failure.

How to diagnose it

  • Separate retired/cleanup lifecycle state from Gateway connectivity and filesystem access.

How to fix it

  • Check the run's artifact_workspaces row (retired flag), any artifact_cleanup_claims entry and the last result in artifact_maintenance. For the 'storage is temporarily unavailable' variant, find the OSError in the Server log for the generated-artifacts directory beside the native state store (under AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR) and fix its permissions, mount or disk space; do not delete registry state to clear the error.
  • Inspect the namespace lifecycle and actual storage/Gateway failure; restore the eligible owning workspace without assuming the files are lost.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported owning workspace is available and its authoritative artifact state is established.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
